emma: quick question — running into a weird embeddings dim mismatch when paginating through a large corpus with our batch helper. hope someone has seen this :sweat_smile:

emma: flow: chunk docs -> tokenize -> batch into fixed size (N) -> client.embeddings.create(...) for each batch. some batches return vectors of length 1536 and others 1024. not consistent per model.

raj: are you sure the model param is the same every call? sometimes a fallback to a different model variant happens if capacity/timeout triggers.

emma: yep explicitly passing model: "rwd-embed-1" in every call. also noticing this happens more when using the pagination helper that yields smaller final batch sizes.

kim: can you paste snippet of the batching code? curious if there's any accidental concat or dtype change.

emma: sure — simplified: ```python
def page_and_embed(docs):
    for page in pager(docs, page_size=100):
        chunks = [tokenize(d) for d in page]
        batches = batch_helper(chunks, batch_size=16)
        for b in batches:
            resp = client.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-1", input=b)
            yield resp.data
```

emma: resp.data sometimes has vectors with len 1024 in the same run.

raj: two quick checks: 1) ensure tokenization isn't returning nested lists for some docs (that could change input shape). 2) check if the SDK is retrying with a different endpoint or model on transient errors. our retry policy can include an alt model in some setups.

kim: also, confirm you're not accidentally passing a single string vs list in some calls. SDK may normalize and choose different internal path.

emma: good call — I logged the exact request payloads. they are consistently lists of strings. no nested arrays.

ci-bot: deploy-check: no recent config changes to default model routing in the last 24h.

raj: another thought — are you mixing quantized model variants across environments? e.g., rwd-embed-1 vs rwd-embed-1-qa. dims would differ.

emma: I grep'd for model names, only rwd-embed-1 in code. but I do see the env var EMBED_MODEL as fallback in one module (old). could be used in pagination helper.

kim: aha, that sounds plausible. pagination helper lives in utils/ and might import different config.

emma: removed the fallback env var and re-ran — all vectors now 1536 consistently. :tada:

raj: nice! follow-ups: 1) add an assert on vector length before consuming. 2) consider making batch_helper include model metadata in logs.

emma: will do. also FYI — while debugging I hit a streaming quirk where the SDK's streaming client would cut a long batch and return a partial frame; filing a tiny bug. anyone seen that?

kim: I've seen streaming chunks split mid-object when network jitter + chunked transfer encoding happens. make sure your streaming consumer reassembles frames and handles retry idempotently.

emma: filing an issue now with repro steps and sample logs. thanks all :pray:

raj: ping me on the PR and I can review the assert/logging change.

emma: thanks!
